verdict.summary: Creating and testing your own Pipedrive OAuth app is quick and self-serve, but Composio has no managed Pipedrive OAuth app, so you must register your own. Going public in the Marketplace requires a review that Pipedrive says can take up to 21 business days, and scope choices are the most likely cause of rejection.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 1-2 days (app setup and Composio configuration, scope trimming, review package including demo video and test accounts)
verdict.time_to_first_connection: Under 1 hour once a developer sandbox exists (you can connect your own account to a draft app)
verdict.approval_wait: None to connect your own account or to run a Live private app; up to 21 business days after submitting a public app for review (Pipedrive's own docs)

gates.name: Draft app in developer sandbox (works for you)
gates.unlocks: Create the app in the Developer Hub, save it as a draft, and connect your own sandbox account through Composio.
limits: A developer sandbox account is required to see the Developer Hub.
Sandbox accounts are limited to five seats by default (community source, not verified against Pipedrive docs).
Sandbox may be deleted if no app is created within 45 days (community source, not verified).
Access tokens expire after 60 minutes and must be refreshed.
Refresh tokens expire after 60 days of non-use.

gates.name: Live private app (invited companies, not listed)
gates.unlocks: Other companies can install the app by link, but it does not appear in the Marketplace.
limits: Not listed in the Marketplace and skips review (community source).
Private apps are not published in the Marketplace (official FAQ).
Some client IDs have returned 'App is not found' to users (community thread).
Company-wide enablement requires a global admin (community source).
Authorize-request step is needed only if installs happen outside the Marketplace.
gates.time_to_reach: Same day as Gate 1, once the app is set to Live

gates.name: Public Marketplace app (reviewed)
gates.unlocks: Listed in the Pipedrive Marketplace and installable by any Pipedrive company.
limits: Review checks install/uninstall flows, OAuth implementation, extensions and listing (community summary).
Reviewers require a demo video, test accounts and a contact during approval.
Public apps must use OAuth 2.0 for authentication and request authorization and must not collect or store a user's API token.
Scope changes after approval go through review and require existing installers to reauthorize.
Developer Agreement reportedly has no listing fee, commission or revenue share (community source).
gates.time_to_reach: Up to 21 business days after submission, plus build and review-package time

steps.title: Create a developer sandbox account
steps.detail: Request a free developer sandbox account from Pipedrive. The Developer Hub is only visible inside a sandbox account, so this is required before any app can be created.
gotchas: Sandbox seat and deletion rules come from a third-party guide and are not verified; create an app promptly so the sandbox is not deleted.
Use the account that will be the test account for the app.

steps.title: Open the Developer Hub
steps.detail: In the sandbox account, go to Settings, click the company name of the sandbox account, and choose Developer Hub from the drop-down menu.

steps.title: Choose the app type deliberately
steps.detail: Pick public or private when creating the app. Pipedrive says the app type cannot be changed later. A private app can be set Live for invited installs without review; a public app goes through review before listing.
gotchas: Community reports conflict on whether a private app can later be converted to public; Pipedrive's docs say the type cannot be changed. Treat the choice as permanent.

steps.title: Create the draft app with name and Redirect URI
steps.detail: Enter an app name and the OAuth callback URL, then save as a draft. These are the only two required fields to save a draft; other fields are validated when you send the app to review.

values.label: App name
values.value: Your app name (choose one you can reuse at review)

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Pipedrive's exact redirect-URI matching rules were not confirmed; use the exact string Composio shows.
Composio's toolkit record lists a v1 default callback, while the authorize probe used v3. Use the value shown in your Composio auth config, not a value copied from older docs.

steps.title: Select OAuth scopes: start with the fewest
steps.detail: Open the OAuth & Access scopes section (per a third-party guide) and enable only the scopes your app's endpoints need. Do not copy Composio's default list unchanged.

values.label: Composio default scopes (trim before use)
values.value: contacts:full, leads:full, mail:full, activities:full, products:full, projects:full

gotchas: Review rejects apps requesting scopes they do not use (community PR).
Users see every scope on the consent page.
mail:full and projects:full are Composio defaults; keep them only if your code calls those endpoints.

steps.title: Map scopes to the endpoints you call
steps.detail: Given your list of Pipedrive API calls, an agent can produce a table mapping each endpoint to the scope it needs, flag scopes with no matching call, and draft the scope justification text required for review.
gotchas: The official scope catalogue was not fetched; confirm each scope name against the Pipedrive API reference before submitting.

steps.title: Enter client ID and secret in Composio
steps.detail: Copy the Client ID and Client secret from the draft app in the Developer Hub and paste them into the Pipedrive auth config in Composio. Composio does not offer managed OAuth for Pipedrive, so this step is required.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: An unknown client_id is rejected by the authorize endpoint with HTTP 401 'unauthorized access'; if you see this, re-check the client ID.

steps.title: Run a test authorization from the correct account
steps.detail: Connect your own sandbox account through Composio while the app is still a draft. Pipedrive says OAuth works in draft mode when accessed from the correct Pipedrive account.
gotchas: Testing from a different Pipedrive account will fail even though the app is valid.

steps.title: Verify token refresh and storage
steps.detail: An agent can check that the connection refreshes the access token after 60 minutes, that refresh works via the token endpoint, and that token columns are at least varchar(768). Confirm the app uses the api_domain returned in the token response for API calls.
gotchas: The api_domain behaviour comes from a community integration guide (Nango); confirm Composio handles it for your account.
A refresh token unused for 60 days expires, so a dormant connection will need reauthorization.

steps.title: Optional: set the app Live for invited installs
steps.detail: If you need other companies to install the app before any public listing, set the private app to Live in the Developer Hub. It will not be listed in the Marketplace and does not go through review.
gotchas: Some client IDs returned 'App is not found' to users in one community thread; test with a second company account before inviting users.
Only a global admin can enable the app for other users in a company.

steps.title: Prepare the review package
steps.detail: An agent can draft the scope justification, an install/uninstall test checklist, a privacy-and-use summary, and a demo-video script covering each scope and key feature. Pipedrive's review checklist lists these items, but official privacy policy and listing asset rules were not found.
gotchas: Official listing requirements (privacy policy, logo, domain verification, minimum installs) were not found; check the Developer Hub form for fields.

steps.title: Record the demo video and set up test accounts
steps.detail: Record a demo video showing how each scope is used and the key features. Provide fully functional, up-to-date test accounts and a contact available during approval.
gotchas: Test accounts must work at review time; a stale sandbox can cause rejection.

steps.title: Convert to public and submit for review
steps.detail: In the Developer Hub, submit the app for review. A community answer says converting a private app to public moves it to draft status, where it must be sent to review and approved before publishing.
gotchas: Conflicts with the rule that app type cannot be changed; confirm in the Developer Hub before relying on conversion.
Public apps must not collect or store a user's API token.

steps.title: Wait for review
steps.detail: Pipedrive says public app reviews may take up to 21 business days, citing demand and vacations. Respond quickly to reviewer questions and keep test accounts live.
gotchas: The rejection reasons come from a community PR and a third-party blog; no official rejection list was found.

steps.title: Plan scope changes after approval
steps.detail: Any scope change on an approved app is sent for review as a pending change, and existing installers are emailed to reauthorize. Batch scope changes to avoid repeated reviews and user reauthorization.
gotchas: Scope changes do not go live until approved and merged.

blockers.symptom: Users see 'App is not found' when connecting some client IDs
blockers.cause: Private apps are not listed in the Marketplace; a community thread reports this for some client IDs.
blockers.fix: Confirm the app is set Live, test the install from a second company account, and contact Pipedrive developer support if it persists.

blockers.symptom: App rejected in review for requesting scopes
blockers.cause: Review rejects apps requesting scopes their functionality does not use; Composio's default list includes mail:full and projects:full.
blockers.fix: Trim scopes to endpoints the app calls, remove unused Composio defaults, and document each scope in the demo video and scope justification.

blockers.symptom: Admin-scoped endpoints return errors or no data
blockers.cause: The admin scope only works when a company admin authorizes the app.
blockers.fix: Have a company admin complete the authorization, or drop admin-scoped features for non-admin installs.

blockers.symptom: Other users cannot enable the app in their company
blockers.cause: Only a global admin can enable an app for other users in the company.
blockers.fix: Ask a global admin to enable the app, or plan the install flow around admin enablement.

blockers.symptom: Existing installers must reauthorize after a scope change
blockers.cause: Adding scopes to a published app emails installers and asks them to reauthorize; the change is held as a pending review.
blockers.fix: Batch scope changes, plan reauthorization messaging, and expect a review cycle before the change goes live.

composio.note: Composio does not offer managed OAuth for Pipedrive. Register your own app in the Pipedrive Developer Hub and paste the Client ID and secret into Composio's OAUTH2 (bring-your-own) auth config. Trim the default scopes to what your app calls. The Composio redirect URI shown in your auth config is the one to paste into the Developer Hub.
